Cancellation year.note: A Times Union article from June 18, 2024 and a WAMC public radio report from June 20, 2024 both say Danskammer Energy withdrew its air permit application on Monday, June 17, 2024. That formally ended the expansion project. The court had upheld the permit denial in June 2022, but the company kept the process open until it withdrew.

Latest Activity.note: The same two news reports date the withdrawal of the air permit application to Monday, June 17, 2024. That is the last activity on the project.

Status Detail.value: air permit denied October 2021, denial upheld by court June 2022, application withdrawn June 2024
Status Detail.note: The two news reports describe the permit denial, the 2022 court ruling that upheld it, and the withdrawal in June 2024. The current text only says appeal denied in 2022, which leaves out the withdrawal.

units.notes: The project was ended by the owner withdrawing its application on June 17, 2024. The August 2026 EIA table has no combined cycle generator for this plant, so there is no generator ID to report. Coordinates could not be confirmed; see the question about location.

qa.recommendation: Remove Roseton Generating Station from Other Name(s) on all five unit rows, after checking it. Roseton has its own plant record.
qa.note: Roseton is a separate, larger oil and gas plant that sits about half a mile downstream, and the two plants were sold together to Dynegy in 2001. The EIA table for August 2026 lists only Danskammer under plant code 2480, with no Roseton generators. I did not change this value as instructed. I found no document that treats the two as one plant.
